messages.subject: blavaan syntax with equality constraints
parts:
Hello!

I am encountering some issues with translating a working lavaan model into blavaan. My starting point is a MGCFA configural invariance model with effects coding (simple example with two groups):

model1 <- 
'FAC =~ 
c(L11,L12)*var1 + 
c(L21,L22)*var2 + 
c(L31,L32)*var3 +
c(L41,L42)*var4 + 
c(L51,L52)*var5

L51 == 5-L11-L21-L31-L41
L52 == 5-L12-L22-L32-L42

var1 ~ c(I11, I12)*1
var2 ~ c(I21, I22)*1
var3 ~ c(I31, I32)*1
var4 ~ c(I41, I42)*1
var5 ~ c(I51, I52)*1

0 == I11+I21+I31+I41+I51
0 == I12+I22+I32+I42+I52'

Running the following gives the desired output, where the loadings average to 1 and the intercepts sum to 0:

model.lavaan <- lavaan(model1,
                       data = dat,
                       group = "g",
                       estimator = "MLM",
                       int.ov.free = TRUE,
                       int.lv.free = TRUE,
                       auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                       auto.var = TRUE, 
                       auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE)

If I apply the exact same model specification using blavaan:

model.blavaan1 <- blavaan(model1,
                          data = dat,
                          int.ov.free = TRUE,
                          int.lv.free = TRUE,
                          auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                          auto.var = TRUE, 
                          auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE,
                          group = "g",
                          target = "jags")

... it does not seem to consider the equality constraints at all, even though the output states that:

Constraints:
                                                                     |Slack|
    L51 - (5-L11-L21-L31-L41)                    0.000
    L52 - (5-L12-L22-L32-L42)                    0.000
    0 - (I11+I21+I31+I41+I51)                    0.000
    0 - (I12+I22+I32+I42+I52)                    0.000

I suspect that it is simply because there is overlap between the equality constraints and the default priors? A working model in JAGS would include something like this to achieve effects coding:

 #Piors, item intercepts
  for(k in 1:K){
alpha[1,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[2,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[3,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[4,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[5,k] ~ dsum(-alpha[1,k],-alpha[2,k],-alpha[3,k],-alpha[4,k])
  }

  #Priors, item loadings
  for(k in 1:K){
lambda[1,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[2,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[3,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[4,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[5,k] ~ dsum(5,-lambda[1,k],-lambda[2,k],-lambda[3,k],-lambda[4,k])
  }

My questions is if this is possible to achieve using the blavaan syntax? I am aware that I can assign individual priors to each parameter, but "dsum" does not seem to affect the jags model output file at all. I have tried different options, but no luck so far.

Any help is much appreciated!

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: blavaan syntax with equality constraints
parts:
Sixten,

Thanks for the report; that constraint specification should have worked. I believe that something changed in lavaan, which caused blavaan to ignore the constraints. It should now be fixed on github, and I will try to get a new version to CRAN soon:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan

One thing about your constraints: instead of 

0 == I11 + I12 + ...

blavaan will want you to put one variable on the lhs:

I11 == -I12 - I13 - ...

The reason is that, in doing the translation to jags, we always need one variable to be a function of others, and blavaan currently isn't smart enough to do that on its own.

Ed

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: blavaan syntax with equality constraints
parts:
Sixten

Adding to this, you can use the measEq.syntax() function from semTools to build the syntax for this types of models with differents types of constraints. And in this case it already defines the first indicator parameter in function of the others, avoiding the issue that Ed mentioned

Here is an example with the HolzingerSwineford1939 data set

mtest <- measEq.syntax('FAC =~ x1+x2+x3+x4+x5',
                       ID.fac = "FX",
                       data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
                       group = "school")
cat(as.character(mtest))


f_test <- bcfa(as.character(mtest),
               data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
               group = "school",
               target = "jags",
               adapt=4000, burnin=15000,sample=5000)
summary(f_test)
